lean_implies_source.reasoning: Under the literal reading of Exercise 2.6.4, the source requires a no-prefactor estimate exp(-c₀t²/V). The Lean conclusion supplies only 2 exp(-ct²/V). For arbitrarily small positive t²/V this latter right side exceeds 1 and provides no route to the strictly subunit no-prefactor bound; the leading 2 cannot be absorbed into a positive universal exponent coefficient uniformly for all t > 0. The competing pragmatic reading of the exercise is an unresolved source-intent ambiguity requiring adjudication.

source_implies_lean.reasoning: For V > 0, a no-prefactor bound exp(-c₀t²/V) immediately implies the Lean bound with the same c₀ because exp(-c₀t²/V) ≤ 2 exp(-c₀t²/V). If V = 0, the Lean interval hypotheses force the centered sum to vanish almost everywhere and its totalized right side is 2, so the Lean conclusion follows trivially even though the source display leaves its own quotient convention unstated.

findings.source_evidence: Theorem 2.2.6 on PDF page 6 / printed page 17 has no leading prefactor, while Exercise 2.6.4 on PDF page 18 / printed page 29 authorizes replacing only the numerical coefficient in the exponent. The rendered Theorem 2.6.3 has absolute-value bars around the complete weighted sum and a leading factor 2.
findings.lean_evidence: D001 bounds the one-sided centered event by 2 * exp(-(c*t²/V)).
findings.impact: On the literal exponent-only reading, the Lean proposition is strictly weaker and does not imply the selected source result. Because the exercise simultaneously directs the reader to deduce the result from a two-sided theorem whose immediate bound retains 2, adjudication is required to resolve whether the book intended the literal no-prefactor contract or tolerated the direct prefactored consequence.

findings.source_evidence: Theorem 2.2.6 gives no positive-total-width hypothesis and no meaning for its quotient when Σ_i(M_i - m_i)² = 0.
findings.lean_evidence: D037 totalizes real division by zero, so D001 evaluates the exponent to zero and the right side to 2 when all widths vanish.
findings.impact: The target's all-singleton case is true because the centered event is null, but its numerical formula is a Lean-specific completion of an unresolved source edge case rather than a source-stated convention.

rationale: All controlled hashes match. Direct inspection of the rendered source confirms that Theorem 2.6.3 is two-sided, with absolute-value bars around the full weighted sum and a leading 2, whereas the referenced Theorem 2.2.6 is one-sided and has no prefactor. The Lean proposition otherwise accurately captures a uniform positive exponent constant, finite independent measurable real variables, almost-sure interval bounds, centering by expectation, positive thresholds, and the squared-width denominator. On the literal wording of Exercise 2.6.4, retaining 2 makes the Lean result weaker, so it is not accepted. Adjudication remains necessary because the exercise's requested exponent-only relaxation conflicts with the visible form of the theorem from which it asks for a deduction, and because the source leaves the zero-total-width quotient undefined while Lean assigns it total real-division semantics.
